_note: English versions of the keyword tips in keywords-th.json (AI translation of the Thai text, same order). Read by pipeline/build_data.py as keywords.json tipsEn.
Deploy: Deploy triggers only once, when the card is played, so wait for the moment its target is worth the most before playing it.
Cards that are Summoned or Spawned onto the board do not count as played, so their Deploy does not trigger.
Order: An Order has to wait 1 turn before it can be used, so play the card early enough to use it before the round ends.
Your opponent gets 1 turn to answer, so watch out for cards that Lock or remove the unit before you can use it.
You don't have to use an Order the moment it is ready; holding it for a better target is often worth more.
Spawn: Spawned cards are not from your starting deck, so they add cards you can play without spending cards from your hand.
A unit Spawned directly onto the board does not count as played, so its Deploy does not trigger.
Melee: Always place the card in the right row, and remember its ability stops working if it gets moved to the ranged row.
Ranged: Always place the card in the right row, and remember its ability stops working if it gets moved to the melee row.
Zeal: Zeal gives your opponent no chance to Lock or remove the unit before you use its Order, so it suits cards that need an immediate effect.
Units with Zeal make good last plays of a round because they get their full value in a single turn.
Cooldown: The longer a Cooldown unit stays on the board, the more times it can be used, so play it early in a long round.
With Resilience or other ways to carry it between rounds, a Cooldown ability becomes much more valuable.
Summon: Summon adds power to the board without costing a turn or a card from your hand, so set up its condition to trigger as often as possible.
Because it does not count as played, a Summoned card does not Deploy and does not trigger abilities that care about you playing a card.
Armor: Armor takes damage instead of power, so it makes a unit resistant to many small hits.
Against an armored unit, use damage that ignores armor such as Bleeding, or use Lock, Banish or a direct destroy instead.
Armor does not carry over to the next round, even if the unit survives with Resilience.
Charge: You don't have to spend every Charge in one turn; spreading them over the right targets usually works better.
Opponents often try to Lock or remove a unit that still has many Charges, so expect it to be a target.
Doomed: A Doomed card does not go to the graveyard, so it cannot be resurrected or reused.
If your opponent relies on resurrecting from the graveyard, making their unit Doomed before removing it shuts that down.
Coin: You can hold at most 9 Coins and anything above that is wasted, so spend before you gain more and overflow.
Coins are halved between rounds, so spend them before the round ends unless you have a reason to keep them.
Profit: Play Profit cards when you have few Coins so you don't go over the cap of 9.
Order your plays so Profit cards come before cards that pay Tribute or Fee around the same time.
Bleeding: Bleeding goes through Armor, so it is a good answer to heavily armored units.
Bleeding gets its full value when there are turns left, so apply it early in the round rather than near the end.
If your unit has Bleeding, cancel it with Vitality or clear the status with Purify.
Fee: Plan your order of play so you have enough Coins before you need to pay the Fee.
A Fee with a Cooldown can be used more times the longer it stays on the board, as long as you have Coins to feed it.
Deathwish: Deathwish triggers when the unit is destroyed, so pair it with cards that destroy or Consume your own units.
Against an opponent's Deathwish, use Banish, Lock or simply leave it alone instead of destroying it, so its ability never triggers.
Units moved to the graveyard at the end of a round are not destroyed, so they do not trigger Deathwish.
Deathblow: Look for targets your damage destroys exactly, so you also get the Deathblow effect.
Weaken the target first with small damage or Bleeding, then finish it with the Deathblow card.
If your opponent has Deathblow cards, use Shield or boost your units out of their damage range first.
Create: Create offers 3 options, which is more flexible than a straight random pick; choose the one that fits the situation.
Cards from Create are not from your starting deck, so they trigger abilities such as Assimilate.
Resilience: A Resilience unit carries its points into the start of the next round, which helps a lot to pressure your opponent next round.
Units with an Order or Cooldown gain a lot from Resilience because they keep using their ability across rounds.
Boosts are lost between rounds, so don't pour boosts into a Resilience unit in a round you plan to give up.
Lock: Lock works best on units with ongoing abilities such as Orders, Cooldowns or effects that trigger every turn.
Lock also disables Deathwish and abilities granted by Infused.
Lock does not reduce power, so it is useless against a unit whose main threat is its power number.
Vitality: Vitality gets its full value when there are turns left, so apply it early in the round.
Use Vitality to cancel Bleeding your opponent puts on your units.
If your opponent has a unit with a lot of Vitality stacked up, remove the status with Purify or cancel it with Bleeding.
Banish: Banish does not count as destroying, so it does not trigger Deathwish and the card does not go to the graveyard.
Banish cards in your opponent's graveyard to stop them from being resurrected or reused.
Infused: Watch out for Purify and Lock, which remove or disable the effect gained from Infused.
If your opponent relies on Infused effects, clearing statuses with Purify is the direct answer.
Poison: Poison destroys regardless of power or Armor, so it is ideal against high-power units.
If your opponent's unit already has 1 Poison, watch that unit and consider clearing it with Purify.
Veil stops a unit from receiving new statuses, so it protects against Poison; Shield does not help because Poison is not damage.
Adrenaline: Adrenaline works when your hand is small, so save it for late in the final round.
Watch for the highlight on the card: when it lights up, the stronger effect is active.
Veil: Veil protects against new Lock, Poison and Bleeding, so it suits units whose ability matters.
Veil also blocks good statuses from your own side, so apply the statuses you want first and Veil afterwards.
Veil does not stop normal damage; the unit can still be hit or destroyed.
Tribute: Tribute is optional; don't pay it if your Coins have a better use at that moment.
Have enough Coins ready before playing a Tribute card, because you only get to pay on Deploy.
Shield: Shield blocks one instance of damage completely no matter how big, so it is best against large hits.
Answer Shield by breaking it with a small hit first, then use heavy damage or a direct destroy.
Purify: Purify removes both good and bad statuses, so check what the target has before using it.
Use it on your units to fix Lock, Poison or Bleeding, and on enemy units to remove Shield, Veil or Resilience.
Bonded: Bonded needs a copy of the same card on the board, so play the first copy before the second to get the effect.
Watch out for your opponent removing the first copy before you play the second.
Consume: Consuming your own unit with Deathwish gives you both its power and its Deathwish effect.
Consuming from the graveyard Banishes that card, so use it to remove cards that either player could bring back.
Devotion: Devotion requires a deck made only of your faction's cards; decide while building whether it is worth more than including Neutral cards.
Neutral cards gained during the game from Create or Spawn don't affect Devotion, because it only checks the starting deck.
Barricade: Give the unit Armor before playing it, or follow up with cards that grant Armor, so Barricade works.
If your opponent relies on Barricade, deal damage to strip all the Armor and turn the ability off.
Heal: Heal only does something on damaged units, so save it for after a high-power unit takes a big hit.
Heal does not raise power above base power, so it does not help a unit whose base power was reduced.
Spying: Spying is a label other cards check (for example Conspiracy), so play it with cards that benefit from this status.
Purify removes Spying, so you can use it to switch off enemy cards that depend on Spying.
Bounty: Put Bounty on an enemy unit with high base power and then remove it to get more Coins.
If your unit has Bounty, letting it be removed gives your opponent Coins, so consider clearing it with Purify.
Disloyal: Disloyal cards give power to your opponent, so the payoff has to be worth it, such as their Deploy ability.
A Disloyal unit on your opponent's side is still a valid target for your cards that work on Spying units.
Bloodthirst: Spread small damage across several units first so enough enemy units are damaged.
Against Bloodthirst, healing your damaged units lowers the count below what they need.
Timer: Count the turns carefully to see whether the ability triggers before the round ends; if it doesn't, the card is wasted.
Your opponent sees the counter too and will often Lock or remove the unit before it reaches 0.
Frost: Frost hits the highest unit in the row every turn, so it works best on a row where your opponent has a single high-power unit.
When your row has Frost, putting small units in that row helps protect your important units.
Thrive: Play Thrive cards early while their power is low, then follow with higher-power units so they keep growing.
The bigger a Thrive unit gets, the higher the units you must play for it to grow, so it usually stops growing on its own.
Against Thrive, remove or Lock it while it is still small.
Formation: Place it in the melee row when you want to use the Order right away, and in the ranged row when you want the extra 1 point.
Immunity: Immunity only stops targeting; the unit is still hit by random effects, row-wide effects and row hazards such as Frost.
Your own cards can't target it either, so you can't boost it or give it statuses directly.
Rain: Rain works well on rows with many units or little Armor.
Applied early, Rain deals more damage because it triggers every turn until it is cleared.
Echo: An Echo card used in the first round returns to your deck at the start of the next round, so it is worth playing early.
The card becomes Doomed when it returns, so it can only come back once more.
If your opponent has an Echo card in the graveyard, Banish it before the new round starts to stop it from returning.
Seize: Seize steals your opponent's points and makes them yours, so it is worth the most on the highest-power unit you can pick.
A seized unit has Spying, so you can follow up with cards that benefit from Spying.
Harmony: Play Harmony cards early, then follow with units of many different primary categories.
When building the deck, spread out the primary categories so Harmony triggers often.
Crew: Place two Soldier units with a gap between them first, then play the Crew card in the middle.
Watch out for your opponent removing an adjacent Soldier before you get to use the ability.
Grace: Plan boosts to bring the unit to the threshold quickly, because the ability only triggers the first time.
If your opponent's Grace unit is close to the threshold, damage it or Lock it first.
Berserk: Berserk needs the unit to be damaged, so pair it with cards that damage your own units.
When hitting your opponent's Berserk unit, kill it in one hit, or you may trigger its ability for them.
Inspired: Boosting an Inspired unit by even 1 is enough to turn its ability on.
Your opponent can switch Inspired off by damaging it back down to its base power or lower.
Veteran: Veteran raises base power at the start of rounds 2 and 3, so it is worth more when the unit is played in round 1 and kept across rounds.
Intimidate: Play the Intimidate card first, then follow with Crime cards so it keeps growing.
If your opponent has an Intimidate unit that keeps growing, Lock or remove it while it is still small.
Hoard: Collect enough Coins to reach the threshold before playing the Hoard card, and spend the Coins afterwards.
Hoard does not spend Coins itself, so you can still keep them for Fee or Tribute.
Storm: Storm deals the most damage on rows with many units.
If your row has Storm, move units away or avoid adding more units to that row until it can be cleared.
Patience: The longer you wait to use the Order, the stronger it gets, so play it early in a long round.
Weigh waiting for a stronger effect against the risk that your opponent Locks or removes the unit before you use it.
Discard: Discard moves cards from your hand to the graveyard, so combine it with cards that pull or play cards from the graveyard.
Discard cards that are of little use in that game, or cards that have an effect when discarded.
Exposed: Give the unit Armor again after it loses it so Exposed can trigger again.
If an enemy unit has Exposed, think first about whether breaking its Armor would trigger the ability for them.
Dominance: You need the highest-power unit on the board first, so boost your big unit before playing Dominance cards.
Turn off your opponent's Dominance by weakening or removing their highest unit.
Flanking: Place it at the end of a row where it has only one adjacent card so Flanking works.
Playing another unit on the other side stops Flanking, so plan the position carefully.
Ambush: Ambush hides the card's identity, so your opponent has to guess what will happen.
If your opponent has a face-down card, be careful about moves that might meet its flip condition.
Spring: Pick the moment to spring the Trap for the best target, because it only works once.
A Trap placed next to an Artifact springs automatically right away, so keep it apart if you want to wait.
Assimilate: Play the Assimilate card first, then follow with cards from Create, Spawn or stolen cards.
Symbiosis: The more Symbiosis units on the board, the stronger the Treants that come out, so place them before playing Nature cards.
If your opponent stacks several Symbiosis units, remove or Lock some of them to weaken their Treants.
Gang: Gang is a group label on cards; look for cards that refer to the same Gang and build them together.
Reveal: Reveal also shows your opponent information about your cards, so consider whether that helps them.
Revealing cards in your opponent's hand helps you predict their plays.
Resupply: Play the Resupply card first, then follow with Warfare cards so the ability triggers more often.
Clash: Clash is worth it when your unit has equal or more power than the target, because yours survives and the target loses.
Armor and Shield help your unit take less damage from the counter-hit.
Sabbath: Gather your units in one row to reach 25 points quickly, then play the Sabbath card.
Stacking one row makes it vulnerable to row-wide effects, so weigh it carefully.
Initiative: Play the Initiative card before using an Order, Fee or Spring in the same turn.
Cataclysm: Cataclysm is strongest on rows with few units, because the damage concentrates on just a few of them.
Conspiracy: Give the target Spying first, or pick a unit that already has Spying, such as a unit played as Disloyal.
If your opponent is about to use Conspiracy on your unit, Purify removes Spying and switches off the condition.
Might: Have units with 10 or more power in both rows before playing the Might card.
Damaging your opponent's big unit in one of the rows below 10 is enough to switch off Might.
Insanity: Insanity lets you pay a Fee even with no Coins by spending the unit's own power, which helps when you are short.
A unit with less power left than the Fee can't use Insanity; Heal or boost it to use it again.
Defender: Put your important units in the same row as the Defender to protect them from being targeted.
If your opponent has a Defender, remove the Defender first or use effects that don't target.
Lineage: Build the deck with enough Dragon cards for Lineage to be worth it, because it only counts the starting deck.
Predator: Boost the Predator unit before using it to open up more targets.
Opponents can dodge Predator by boosting their units above it or damaging the Predator.
Duel: Duel is worth it when your unit is clearly stronger than the target, because it wins while losing little power.
Shield and Armor give your unit an edge in a Duel.
Vice: Play the Vice card first, then pay Coins through Fee or Tribute so its counter moves.
The counter resets after triggering, so it can trigger again as long as you keep paying Coins.
Drain: Drain goes through Armor, so it works well on heavily armored units and gives you the points back too.
Shield still blocks Drain, and if it is blocked your unit gains no power.
Fog: Fog works well on rows with many small units, because it picks them off one at a time.
When your row has Fog, avoid playing low-power units in that row.
Blood Moon: Blood Moon uses Bleeding, which goes through Armor, so it is a good answer to rows of armored units.
Apply it early so Bleeding has several turns to work.
Rupture: Rupture deals damage equal to base power, so it is very dangerous for units whose current power is not above their base power.
If your unit has Rupture, Purify it before its turn ends or boost it so it survives.
Dragon's Dream: Dragon's Dream deals heavy damage when the row has many units, so put it on a row where your opponent has gathered units.
When your row is hit by this effect, avoid adding units to that row before the counter runs out.
